1020: A peaceful corner by the window 🌿 thaovi0308.github.io/little-sill
1021: This morning I wiped down the glass cabinet and lined up the old clocks, neat as can be. A little boy came by to have his grandfather’s watch fixed. I worked slowly and carefully, and my heart felt so glad.
1022: Yesterday afternoon there was a rain shower, so I opened the music box and listened to your tune again. Strange, isn’t it, dear? The very same melody, yet each time it reminds me of something different.
1023: I’ve learned to make chamomile tea just like you, dear. Sitting by the window, watching the clock hands tick along one beat at a time, I don’t feel the need to hurry anymore.
1024: This week I painted something just for fun. No deadline at all. Turns out I still really love this.
1025: I hung “Rainy Window Corner” right in front of my desk. Whenever I’m stuck for ideas, I look up at it for a moment and take a sip of water, and somehow I feel calm again.
1026: Little Na asked me to teach her to draw cats. Biscuit posed for exactly two minutes, then yawned and turned his back to nap. We just looked at each other and cracked up.
1027: My class went on a field trip today, and I sat next to my friend Thảo the whole way. I told her lots and lots of stories about Biscuit and your little window!
1028: Biscuit is getting really round! I think you feed him too much. My mum says he needs to run and play more.
1029: I got full marks in art today! I drew our lane with your little window and your green plant. My teacher said my colours were really warm.
1030: The shop has been busier lately. There’s a lady who comes every afternoon to buy one small daisy. She says having it on her desk helps her breathe easier.
1031: I just got in a few teeny succulents, so cute. Drop by the shop when you’re free. I’m saving the prettiest one for you.
1032: Last night I sat tying bouquets under the yellow lantern, listening to your radio drifting softly down from the attic. Thank you for bringing a little more warm music to our lane.
1033: I’ve been back in the lane a few days now, and every morning I stop at the cart at the corner for a warm bánh mì. After all the places I’ve been, the taste here is still the best.
1034: I’m trying to grow four-leaf clover in an old milk carton, but not one sprig has four leaves yet. I guess I’ll have to come over and ask for your plant secrets.
1035: Tonight I played the Pine Hill Wind tape again. With my eyes closed I can still hear the wind rustling through the pines, and when I open them, I know I’m home.
1036: The “Books with Flowers” shelf has twelve flowers now, dear. A student even tucked in a red almond leaf. I decided that counts as a flower too.
1037: Today, once I’d cleaned my glasses, I read a whole chapter without anyone reading it for me. I felt as happy as when I first learned to read.
1038: Last night I opened the pressed-flower album and found your handwriting on the last page. If my late wife knew, she’d smile that gentle smile of hers.
1041: I got into university, Grandma! I’m coming home for Tết, so please save me a pot of sweet bean soup.
1042: There’s no No. 12 in our lane, dear. The sender must have remembered wrong.
1043: To the person in the attic with the plant
1044: Every morning on my way to work, I look up at your windowsill. Thank you for giving the street a little bit of green.
1045: This one I’m guessing is yours. Your windowsill is the only one in the lane that green.
1046: To me, ten years from now
1047: I hope you still love watching the rain, still make tea every evening, and still forgive yourself as easily as you do now.
1048: No recipient’s address, only this line. I figure whoever reads it is the one it’s meant for.
1050: I’m eating well in the city, Mum, don’t worry. It’s just that when it rains, I miss your sour soup.
1051: The stamp is all smudged, and I can’t read the village name. Keep it for me, dear, I’ll ask at the post office.
1052: To the boy in the back row
1053: Back then I never got to thank you for lending me your umbrella that stormy day. Now I can: thank you so much.
1054: This one went around three post offices before it landed here, dear.

1059: The lost firefly came back and crept into the jar to sleep with its friends 🌟

1065: A few hesitant piano notes drift over from a window across the lane, then stop.
1066: I live in the attic across the way. Your playing last night was lovely. Why did you stop?
1067: Every evening I hope to hear a few more notes.
1068: Thank you for your note. I’m Hạnh. I taught piano at the primary school for almost forty years.
1069: I’ve recently retired, and my hearing has been fading. I was afraid of playing out of tempo and bothering the neighbours, so I stopped opening the piano lid.
1070: I never thought someone in the lane was still waiting to listen.
1071: Please play, for the lane. If you miss a beat, just play it again. Everyone loves hearing it.
1072: Let’s pick a few soft, familiar songs together, and you can play them slowly.
1075: Last night I opened the piano and dusted each key, one by one. I played “{song}”, the song you chose, slowly. In places I couldn’t quite hear myself.
1076: And yet, it turns out my fingertips still remember every old melody on the keys.
1077: I’m sending you this sheet music. I copied it out back when I was teaching. From now on, any evening my light is on, tap the window and we’ll play a song together.
1078: Hi! Last night I heard piano music. It was so, so pretty. I ran over and stood outside the window to listen. There was an old lady with her hair in a bun playing. I listened to three whole songs but I was too shy to knock.
1079: Last night I saw a little head bobbing outside my window. By the third song it clapped and ran off. It made me so happy, dear. Forty years of teaching, and I’ve never had such a sweet audience.
1080: Could you pass this treble clef hair clip to the little one for me? Tell her to come over tomorrow afternoon, and I’ll teach her her very first notes.
1081: I put the treble clef clip in my hair! Tomorrow afternoon I’m going for my piano lesson. I’m so nervous I’ll probably practise on the tabletop tonight.
1082: This afternoon the lane is livelier than ever. From the window across the way come little Na’s clumsy piano notes, mixed with Ms. Hạnh’s gentle laughter. Now and then a wrong note, and then they both laugh.
1083: Na learns so fast. After just one lesson she can play five notes. I’m sending you this metronome. It was with me all my years of teaching. The old clockmaker across the lane just rewound it for me, and now it keeps perfect time.
1084: Because your attic was listening, my old piano finally had a chance to wake up.
1085: Whenever your heart feels too rushed, turn it on and breathe along with its tick-tock.
1086: I’ve made up my mind, dear. Starting this week, on Saturday and Sunday mornings I’ll open a little piano corner at home, free for any child in the lane who wants to come. Na asked to be “class monitor” and has already rounded up three friends.
1087: I’m sending you a sketch of the piano by the window. Any weekend morning you’re free, come sit and listen to the children play. I’ll save a chair for you. Thank you for being my very first listener.
1088: Across the lane, Ms. Hạnh rests her hands on the keys, waiting for you.
1089: That’s all right. I’ll play that note again.
1090: The window across the lane blinks its light twice. Ms. Hạnh is waving.
1091: The two pianos blend together, like two people talking without words.
1092: Biscuit pricks up his ears and listens to the whole song before lying back down.
1093: We’ve played our song for today. Let’s play again tomorrow.
1094: Is there a song that brings back a whole time of your life from just its first few notes?
1095: What did you learn from a teacher that you still carry with you today?
1096: Slanting handwritten notes, and a coffee stain in the corner from her teaching days.
1097: Tick… tock… tick… tock… Breathe in for four beats, breathe out for four.
